name: Citizenship by Descent / Birth

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 23: anyone born in Honduran territory is a Honduran national by birth (excluding children of accredited foreign diplomats). The same article covers those born aboard Honduran-flagged military or merchant vessels in Honduran waters, and foundlings of unknown parentage found in Honduras.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad to a Honduran-by-birth parent

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 23: a person born abroad to a Honduran parent who is themselves Honduran by birth acquires Honduran nationality. The source reviewed for this build did not specify a residence or registration formality to perfect this, or whether it applies equally regardless of which parent is Honduran -- both read gender-neutral in the constitutional text itself.
requirements.fix_path: Register the birth with a Honduran consulate or civil registry as the child of a Honduran-by-birth parent.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Honduran nationality by birth

sources.title: Georgetown University Political Database of the Americas -- hosted text of Honduras's 1982 Constitution, Title II Chapter I (nationality), Articles 23-24

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Honduras). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an academic-hosted (Georgetown University) copy of the Constitution, tier 2, not a Honduran government domain directly; Honduras's own official gazette (La Gaceta) hosting of this text was not located in this build. GENUINE, GENDER-NEUTRAL FINDING: unlike several other countries built in this dataset (Syria, Guatemala's older descent framing), Article 23's language for both jus soli and descent reads as gender-neutral on its face -- no father/mother asymmetry found in the text reviewed. dual_citizenship_allowed set true per Article 24's treaty-dependent dual-nationality mechanism (see hn_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes for the fuller picture, including the confirmed 1966 Spain treaty) -- disclosed as treaty-dependent rather than a universal right, since Article 24 only guarantees it 'when a double nationality treaty exists' with the other country.
